sea noun

also the deep, the main, the open sea

classical

Traupman 206

mare, maris n.

noun, third declension

Other words

  • aequor, aequoris n. — the level sea; any level surface

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Varr. LL 7.23: aequor mare appellātum, quod aequātum, cum commōtum ventō nōn est (Lewis & Short); Lucr. 4.106: speculōrum aequor (Lewis & Short)

    (vōx poētica: Lucr., Verg.)

    From aequus, level: the plain of the sea when no wind stirs it, and so the sea. A poets’ word before Augustus; once in Cicero and once in Sallust (Lewis & Short).

  • pontus, pontī m. — the sea

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Verg. A. 3.193: caelum undique et undique pontus (Lewis & Short); Lucr. 2.559 (Lewis & Short)

    (vōx poētica: Lucr., Verg.)

    Greek πόντος, the poets’ word for mare (Lewis & Short).

  • pelagus, pelagī n. — the open sea, the main

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Verg. A. 5.8: pelagus tenuēre ratēs (Lewis & Short); Hor. C. 1.3.11 (Lewis & Short)

    (vōx poētica: Lucr., Verg., Hor.; also post-Augustan prose)

    Greek πέλαγος; a neuter in -us.

Examples

  • caelum undique et undique pontus

    sky on every side and on every side the seaVerg. A. 3.193 (Lewis & Short)

  • pelagus tenuēre ratēs

    the ships held the open seaVerg. A. 5.8 (Lewis & Short)

See also wave, sailor, ship.
